This is the curated research evidence dossier for **Daily Digest for Muki** (Issue 018, July 27, 2026), compiled after analyzing and verifying the strongest cultural signals from the past 24 to 72 hours.

---

### Candidate 1: Visual Culture Signal (Exhibitions, Photobooks)

*   **Proposed Section**: Visual Culture Signal
*   **Exact Title**: CPW: Bound: The Making of a Photobook
*   **Specific Source URL**: `https://cpw.org/exhibitions/bound-the-making-of-a-photobook/`
*   **Event/Publication Date**: July 11 – August 9, 2026
*   **Verified Facts**: 
    *   **What happened**: The Center for Photography at Woodstock (CPW) is hosting a unique exhibition titled *Bound: The Making of a Photobook* in its new Community Gallery.
    *   **Scope & Material**: The exhibition focuses on the physical, iterative craft of photobook making—tracing projects from early book dummies to final publications. It reveals the hidden, non-linear stages of design compromise, experimentation, and layout.
    *   **Artists & Educators**: It features student-made photobooks from workshops taught over the last year by prominent photographic artists Raymond Meeks, Adrianna Ault, and Vladimir Nahitchevansky, alongside senior thesis photobooks from Bard College’s Photography Program.
*   **Relevance to Muki**: Directly supports research into the physical materiality of the photobook medium and its curatorial/academic production workflows. It demystifies the tactile labor of photobook "dummies" as sites of spatial and structural experimentation.
*   **Duplication Assessment**: New. No prior mentions of CPW, Raymond Meeks, or this exhibition.

### Candidate 2: AI Research / Creative Tech Signal

*   **Proposed Section**: AI Research / Creative Tech Signal
*   **Exact Title**: Breakdowns for Human-Machine Creative Reflexivity
*   **Specific Source URL**: `https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.15866`
*   **Publication Date**: July 17, 2026
*   **Verified Facts**:
    *   **What happened**: Researchers Marianne Bossema (Amsterdam University of Applied Sciences/Leiden University), Somaya Ben Allouch, and Rob Saunders published a critical paper on human-AI collaborative design. It was presented at the inaugural *Reflection in Creative Experience* (RiCE) Workshop in London on July 13, 2026.
    *   **Technical & Design Mechanism**: The paper critiques the current trend of using GenAI for "goal-directed, automated content generation," which reduces human creators to mere "curators of AI outputs". Instead, the authors propose designing deliberate **"breakdowns"** (system-induced friction, pauses, and disruptions in the workflow) to prompt human reflection-in-action, preserve human creative agency, and maintain a reciprocal, non-linear dialogue between human and machine. 
    *   **Target Group**: The framework was tested during collaborative drawing experiments, specifically focusing on older adults, who are highly vulnerable to feeling a loss of control when interacting with autonomous systems.
*   **Relevance to Muki**: Crucial framework for Muki's AI-native creative workflows. It offers a sophisticated, anti-neoliberal, and human-centered design philosophy that resists the mindless "outsourcing" of creative labor, introducing "friction" as a tool for cognitive autonomy and care.
*   **Duplication Assessment**: New. This paper and the RiCE workshop have not been covered in prior digests.

### Candidate 3: Feminist Structure Signal (Women, Labor, Care, Bodies)

*   **Proposed Section**: Feminist Structure Signal
*   **Exact Title**: Nancy Bowen: From A to Z and the Bodies In Between
*   **Specific Source URL**: `https://www.nunufineart.com/exhibitions/nancy-bowen-from-a-to-z-and-the-bodies-in-between`
*   **Exhibition/Review Date**: June 5 – July 25, 2026 (Whitehot Magazine review published on July 24, 2026).
*   **Verified Facts**:
    *   **What happened**: Whitehot Magazine published an in-depth review of second-wave feminist artist Nancy Bowen's first solo show at Nunu Fine Art in SoHo. 
    *   **Scope & Material**: Bowen (b. 1955), who describes herself as an **"artistic archaeologist,"** creates collages and sculptures that physically dismantle patriarchal linguistic and visual structures. 
    *   **Specific Artworks**: She layers geometric patterns, pigment, and glitter over vintage dictionary pages sourced from her late parents’ home. In her sculptures (like *From the Deep*, 2024), she combines ceramics, wax, pigmented paper pulp, porcupine quills, and her mother's vintage seashell collection to evoke the female body (such as the historical Venus motif) while actively resisting literal or domestic classification.
*   **Relevance to Muki**: Intersects feminist visual culture, somatic mediums, and the archiving of private grief/family materials. Bowen’s "artistic archaeology" offers an inspiring method of using vernacular paper archives (dictionaries) to rewrite gendered language.
*   **Duplication Assessment**: New.

### Candidate 4: China / East Asia Signal

*   **Proposed Section**: China / East Asia Signal
*   **Exact Title**: Jianquan Li: Echo of Being | UMPRUM
*   **Specific Source URL**: `https://www.umprum.cz/en/web/departments/fine-arts/fine-arts-iv/jianquan-li-echo-of-being`
*   **Exhibition Date**: July 3 – 31, 2026
*   **Verified Facts**:
    *   **What happened**: Prague-based Chinese artist Jianquan Li is presenting his MA diploma exhibition *Echo of Being* at the Atrium Žižkov Gallery in Prague, Czech Republic.
    *   **Structure & Material**: The core of the project is a hand-bound photobook created using traditional Chinese binding. The book is designed with two covers and two reading directions, giving the viewer two interconnected, non-linear narratives where domestic spaces, light, and the human body become memory repositories. 
    *   **Spatial Extension**: The exhibition expands the photobook format into a physical installation. Photographs are projected onto a translucent chiffon fabric screen, where images overlap with shadows and respond to the physical movement of the air, accompanied by an ambient musical composition.
*   **Relevance to Muki**: An exemplary East Asian diasporic artistic practice that combines photography, media archaeology (traditional Chinese binding), and spatial-tactile curating to archive memory and intimacy.
*   **Duplication Assessment**: New.

### Candidate 5: Archive / Long Read / Opportunity

*   **Proposed Section**: Archive / Long Read / Opportunity
*   **Exact Title**: LensCulture Photobook Prize 2026
*   **Specific Source URL**: `https://www.lensculture.com/photo-competitions/photobook-prize-2026`
*   **Deadline Date**: Call open July 8 – August 12, 2026 (Early-bird submission discount ends July 29, 2026).
*   **Verified Facts**:
    *   **What happened**: LensCulture has officially opened submissions for its inaugural Photobook Prize 2026.
    *   **The Opportunity**: The winning photographer will receive a fully-funded book publication and worldwide distribution through the prestigious Nazraeli Press (valued at over $25,000, print run of 500 copies plus 50 artist copies).
    *   **Exhibition & Jury**: The winner, along with 5 shortlisted photographers (who also receive $500 grants), will have their work exhibited at SHOWLA in Los Angeles in December 2026. The jury features influential publishers, including Chris Pichler (Nazraeli Press), Gianluca Gamberini (L'Artiere), Rachel Barker (Stanley/Barker), and Clint Woodside (Deadbeat Club). No book dummy is required for submission.
*   **Relevance to Muki**: A highly practical, top-tier international opportunity in contemporary photobook publishing. The impending early-bird discount deadline (July 29, 2026) makes it extremely timely for Muki’s network of photographers and researchers.
*   **Duplication Assessment**: New. No prior mentions of the LensCulture Photobook Prize.
